Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 99, English)
The Sunday Mool Tatva Session: Dimensions, Parallel Universes, and the "30%" Teaching on Karma and Destiny

This session opens as a general Sunday Mool T atva session (distinct fr om the Thir d Eye advanced batch), welcoming newcomers, then delivers an extended dimension/mantra-physics lectur e originally taught to the Thir d Eye batch, befor e pivoting into a detailed teaching on why some people's efforts never seem to "complete," illustrated by the speaker's own astr ological story .
Part A — Opening, Welcome, and a Suggestion Box Discussion
1. Session opening: The speaker opens with a warm welcome to Ashaeiynn on a Sunday , noting that today a Third Eye batch has just completed and a new batch will begin shortly after this session.

2. A devotee's r equest for a structur ed query form: A devotee (32 years old, from a Radhaswami family background, the first in his family to adopt murti puja) shares that he joined Ashaeiynn about a month ago after independently researching who to take as a guru, and felt led here by providence. He requests a structured form/application where devotees can submit questions in advance, since with 150–200 people in a session, one-on-one questions take too long.

3. Why a blanket public form isn't simply r eopened: The speaker explains this provision existed in an earlier version of the app and will be reintroduced, but cautions that open-ended anonymous forms tend to be misused by attention-seekers who ask provocative or needling questions specifically because they're afraid to ask openly — whereas someone with a genuine question is not afraid to ask it in front of everyone and generally gets an answer precisely because their question is sincere.

4. Alternative in the meantime: Devotees are encouraged to call the helpline directly with questions; if a call or message goes unanswered, they are told to follow up directly , since detailed records of every devotee's data, audio, and prior questions are maintained.
5. Third Eye batch just completed: The speaker confirms today marks the completion of a Third Eye batch cycle and welcomes first-time attendees to the general Mool Tatva session.
Part B — Ashaeiynn's Identity and Lineage (Recap for Newcomers)

1. What Ashaeiynn is about: Ashaeiynn is described as dedicated entirely to work that opens spiritual vision (dristi) and strengthens the subtle world (sookshm jagat) — explicitly not about external objects like crystals or salt water , but about awakening guru shakti.

2. Lineage and mantra: Ashaeiynn is described as a community of Ram bhakts within the Nath sampradaya, whose guru is Hanuman ji Maharaj, guided by Mata Sita. The core mantra is "Jai Siyaram" — its rishi is Sita Mata, beej is "Raam," shakti is
"Rim," keelak is "Room," and it is set in the Gayatri chhand.
3. Daily and cyclical practice: Per this teaching, devotion happens 24 hours a day at Ashaeiynn — daily negativity-clearing sessions and Ram havan, a monthly Maha Havan, and a yearly Mahotsav .

4. What happens at Ashaeiynn (as described to newcomers): The speaker lists phenomena described as commonplace there — naming deities, reading people's thoughts, seeing past/present/future, perceiving distant events, and even perceiving internal body structures (blood vessels, bones, DNA) — all attributed solely to the strength of saints, mantra shakti, and the guru tattva of Hanuman ji Maharaj seated at the community's guru-position.
5. Stated purpose: The stated goal is to awaken each devotee's past-life powers so they can discover this life's purpose and receive guidance through saints in service of that.

6. The congr egational sankalp prayer: The speaker leads the same standard sankalp prayer used elsewhere in Ashaeiynn's practice — addressed to Hanuman ji Maharaj, naming "Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya" as witness, of fering one's jaap, and asking for acceptance, refuge, awakened vision, and Ram bhakti.

7. Real "miracle" r eframed: The speaker teaches that the real miracle is not dristi itself but asking for bhakti (devotion) even before asking for dristi — fully surrendering to Hanuman ji Maharaj as guru in thought, word, and deed before anything else is sought.

8. How guidance is r eceived: The speaker clarifies he does not literally converse with Hanuman ji Maharaj; rather , through the grace of saints, he perceives Hanuman ji Maharaj's indications, who is described as present in the community in a semimanifest ("ardh pratyaksh"), awakened state.
Part C — The Dimensions and Mantra-Physics Teaching (Repeated for the General Audience)

1. Why this is being r etaught her e: The speaker notes this framework was already taught in the Third Eye advanced batch, but is bringing a version of it to the general Mool Tatva audience so more devotees can understand it.

2. Kundalini as an infinity loop: As before, kundalini shakti is illustrated as a serpent-like form that, when straightened, resembles the infinity symbol (∞) — an endless loop that can never fully be broken, only shifted in plane.

3. Chakras and dimensions: Per this teaching, each ascending "dimension" (imagined as a floor/step) carries more chakras than the last — 14 at one level, 32 at the next, 64 above that, and so on, continuously increasing.

4. "Up" and "down" ar e relative to the observer: Using multiple devotees seated at dif ferent points around a spherical earth as an example, the speaker teaches that what looks like "up" or "down" is entirely a matter of the observer's position — there is no universal up or down, only relative position.

5. Mantra's staged dimensional r each: The speaker teaches that mantra operates dif ferently depending on which "dimension" it reaches: in the 1st dimension a mantra can only move forward and backward (this covers most ordinary/tamasic mantras); in the 2nd it can also move up and down; in the 3rd it becomes "jagrit" (awakened, producing physical ef fect); in the 4th it can move forward and backward in time itself; in the 5th it can additionally move into parallel universes; and in the 6th it becomes omnipresent, able to act in every direction from every point simultaneously .

6. Parallel universes and healing: The speaker illustrates the 5th-dimension concept with an example of two terminally ill patients: when neither this-world outcome can help, a saint's mantra shakti may draw on a healthier outcome from a parallel version of that same person's life — what looks like "God's blessing" is reframed as this parallel-universe intervention, made possible by suf ficiently intense, repeated mantra practice.

7. Jurisdiction and boundaries between parallel selves: A person may freely draw from their own parallel-universe selves, but attempting to draw from someone else's parallel universe invites correction from the presiding deities of that jurisdiction — described as acting much like unnoticing police who intervene once a violation is noticed.

8. Distance, speed, and r epetition: The speaker frames mantra travel using a distance/speed/time relationship: to cover more dimensional "distance" a mantra needs more speed, and speed comes specifically from repetition (japa count) — not from the mantra's inherent nature alone. This is why an old, deeply established mantra like "Jai Siyaram" is said to require at least one crore (ten million) repetitions before it becomes fully "awakened" and correspondingly fast-acting.

9. Gods and their associated dimensions: Per this teaching, Brahma is associated with roughly the 8th–9th dimension, Vishnu with the 9th–10th, and Lord Shiva with the 10th, described as being present at up to ten places simultaneously; Hanuman ji Maharaj is associated with the 6th dimension in his awakened state, yet is described as having "controlled" a still-higher (14thdimension) power through his own guru's practice — illustrating that dimension level and relative spiritual authority are not the same thing.

10. Same plane, similar experience — a caution against comparing years of practice: The speaker teaches that two practitioners on the "same plane," regardless of how many years each has practiced (e.g., 4 years versus 40), can have essentially the same spiritual experience — cautioning devotees against assuming more years of practice automatically means a categorically dif ferent experience.
Part D — Why Some Efforts Never "Complete" (The Karma/Dosha Teaching)
(This part continues dir ectly from the same live session, with no new opening — pr ompted by devotees asking why their efforts consistently stall.)

1. Two br oad categories of people, by task completion: The speaker teaches there are two broad types: those whose undertakings complete, and those whose undertakings do not — and within each, further sub-categories exist.
2. Instant completion: Those whose favorable planets (notably Surya, Guru, Shukra, or Mangal) align see their ef forts complete quickly and their practices readily accepted.

3. Delayed-but-eventual completion: Those with partially favorable planets need both planetary alignment and sustained personal force (ef fort); with patience, their work does eventually complete as planets align over time.

4. Good start, no finish: A third group starts well (they have some driving force) but cannot complete — described as often deeply frustrated and confused, since they visibly have capability yet cannot finish what they start.

5. No r eal start at all: A fourth group can't even properly begin — described as people whose underlying "backbone" (planetary foundation) is either extremely strong or extremely weak, with nothing in between.
6. What planets r epresent in this framework: Planets (grah) are likened to a "government" — an executing body , not the ultimate source of doshas (af flictions) themselves.

7. Where doshas actually come fr om: Per this teaching, a dosha (af fliction) originates as a "shraap" (curse) — cosmic ener gy one person directs at another (typically as consequence for a wrong committed against them), which is then registered and executed through the planetary "government," appearing on a birth chart as af flictions like Kaal Sarp Dosh, Mangal Dosh, Shani Dosh, Pitru Dosh, and similar .

8. Doshas don't touch a person's underlying "dimension": The speaker clarifies that no planet or government-like force raises or lowers a person's fundamental dimension (spiritual standing) — only other people (through curses/blessings) af fect that; dimension is instead given "as a gift" during the cursing/blessing process and then merely executed by the planets.
9. Doshas exist in light, medium, and extr eme severity , and combinations of multiple doshas can compound into especially dif ficult life patterns.

10. A first-person illustration: The speaker shares his own astrological story as a direct example: he describes a severely af flicted chart (weak Mangal, weak Chandra, absent Surya, absent Guru kripa, Kaal Sarp Dosh, and — confirmed live by a community astrologer , Neelam Shivam — currently running a dif ficult Rahu Mahadasha with Shani Antardasha), such that nothing he attempted, including his own sadhna, would complete beyond roughly 30%.

1 1. Giving up on "karma," then giving up on giving up: After repeated failure at ordinary ef fort (karma), he stopped acting entirely for a period, then turned to jaap instead — reasoning that speech itself is a form of action — but even this stalled at the same ~30% mark.

12. Accepting the 30% and multiplying it: Rather than continuing to strain toward 100% (something his own astrologer told him was structurally impossible for his chart), he accepted his 30% capacity and instead repeated it 300 times, then continued further to roughly 3,000 times.

13. The turning point — a partnership offer ed: At a certain point, per this account, the accumulated intensity of his repeated 30% ef fort became so great that divine forces ef fectively of fered a partnership: "you do your 30%, we will do the remaining 70%" — because his repeated, multiplied 30% had become many times greater than an ordinary person's full, unmultiplied 100%.

14. The lesson — r epeat, don't just attempt once: The core teaching drawn from this account is not to treat any sadhna as a onetime attempt; if a person's natural capacity is limited, the answer is to multiply the attempt (repeat the sadhna as many times as needed, e.g., an 1 1-day sadhna repeated 1 1 or more times) rather than to abandon it as hopeless.

15. Closing framing — "W elcome to the 30%": The speaker frames this as the actual foundation of Ashaeiynn's approach: he says he deliberately keeps close those who, like him, are working from a limited ("30%") starting position rather than those whose charts are already favorable, since their needs and approach dif fer.
16. Session close: The session closes with repeated "Jai Siyaram" and "Jai Gurudev" chanting; a devotee's own sankalp is confirmed as received before the session ends.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Genuine questions are best asked openly (in session or via the helpline) rather than through anonymous forms, which tend to be misused for attention-seeking rather than sincere inquiry . Ashaeiynn's core mantra is "Jai Siyaram," with Sita Mata as rishi, "Raam" as beej, "Rim" as shakti, "Room" as keelak, set in Gayatri chhand. The real "miracle" is asking for bhakti (devotion) before asking for dristi (vision) — full surrender comes first. Mantra's reach expands by dimension: 1st (forward/backward), 2nd (+up/down), 3rd (awakened/physical ef fect), 4th (+time), 5th (+parallel universes), 6th (omnipresence). Mantra "speed" (dimensional reach) comes from repetition count, not from the mantra alone — old, powerful mantras like "Jai Siyaram" need roughly a crore of repetitions to fully awaken. A person may draw on their own parallel-universe selves freely , but not on another person's, without inviting correction. Planets function as an executing "government"; doshas (af flictions) originate as curses from another person's wronged ener gy , not as arbitrary punishment from the planets themselves. No external force can raise or lower a person's underlying spiritual "dimension" — only another person's curse or blessing does that; dimension is a gift given at that moment, then merely carried out by the planets.

If a chart or life circumstance caps a person's capacity (e.g., at "30%"), the answer is to repeat the ef fort many times over rather than abandon it — repetition, not raw capacity , is what eventually invites divine partnership.
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 99, English)
The Sunday Mool Tatva Session: Dimensions, Parallel Universes, and the "30%" Teaching on Karma and Destiny
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Sunday Mool T atva session, covering the dimensions/mantra-physics teaching and the karma/dosha "30%" teaching.

Q1. Why doesn't Ashaeiynn simply r eopen an open, anonymous question form for everyone? A: Per this teaching, open anonymous forms tend to attract attention-seekers asking provocative questions precisely because they're afraid to ask openly , while genuinely sincere questions are rarely held back and tend to get answered when asked directly .

Q2. What should a devotee do if they have a question and can't ask it live in a large session? A: Per this teaching, they're encouraged to call the helpline directly; if there's no response, they should follow up, since detailed records of every devotee's prior communications are kept.
Q3. What is Ashaeiynn's cor e mantra, and what ar e its components? A: "Jai Siyaram" — with Sita Mata as its rishi, "Raam" as beej, "Rim" as shakti, "Room" as keelak, set in the Gayatri chhand.

Q4. Is Ashaeiynn's practice based on external objects like crystals or salt water? A: No — per this teaching, it is explicitly not about such objects; it is about awakening guru shakti through devotion, saints, and Gurudev .

Q5. What is described as happening r egularly at Ashaeiynn? A: Per this teaching, phenomena described as commonplace there include naming deities, reading thoughts, perceiving past/present/future, seeing distant events, and even perceiving internal body structures — attributed to mantra shakti and the guru tattva of Hanuman ji Maharaj.

Q6. What is the r eal "miracle," according to this teaching? A: Asking for bhakti (devotion) even before asking for dristi (vision) — full surrender to the guru in thought, word, and deed, prior to seeking any specific spiritual result.

Q7. Does the speaker claim to literally converse with Hanuman ji Maharaj? A: No — per this teaching, he clarifies he perceives Hanuman ji Maharaj's indications through the grace of saints, describing Hanuman ji Maharaj as present in a semi-manifest, awakened state rather than in direct verbal conversation.
Q8. In this teaching's framework, how does a mantra behave in the first dimension? A: It can only move forward and backward — most ordinary (tamasic) mantras operate only at this level.
Q9. What changes about a mantra at the third dimension? A: It becomes "jagrit" (awakened) — meaning it begins producing a physical, real-world ef fect.

Q10. What can a mantra do once it r eaches the fourth dimension? A: Per this teaching, it can move events forward or backward in time — bringing a future occurrence earlier or drawing a past occurrence forward.

Q1 1. What becomes possible at the fifth dimension? A: Per this teaching, the mantra can reach into parallel universes — illustrated with an example of terminally ill patients whose outcome might be drawn from a healthier parallel version of their life through suf ficiently intense mantra practice.
Q12. What does it mean for a mantra to r each the sixth dimension? A: It becomes omnipresent — able to act simultaneously from every point in every direction at once.

Q13. Can a person draw on someone else's parallel-universe outcomes fr eely? A: No — per this teaching, a person may draw on their own parallel-universe selves freely , but attempting to draw on another person's invites correction from that jurisdiction's presiding deities.

Q14. What determines how "far" or "fast" a mantra can travel dimensionally? A: Per this teaching, it is repetition (japa count), not the mantra's inherent nature alone — described using a distance/speed/time relationship.

Q15. Why does the mantra "Jai Siyaram" r eportedly r equire roughly a cr or e of r epetitions to fully awaken? A: Per this teaching, because it is a very old, deeply established mantra, achieving full dimensional speed/reach requires that volume of repetition.

Q16. According to this teaching, which dimensions ar e Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva associated with? A: Roughly the 8th–9th (Brahma), 9th–10th (V ishnu), and 10th (Shiva) — with Shiva described as present at up to ten places simultaneously .

Q17. Does mor e years of spiritual practice always mean a categorically differ ent experience than fewer years? A: Not necessarily — per this teaching, two practitioners on the "same plane," regardless of years practiced, can have essentially the same experience; the plane matters more than raw years.

Q18. What ar e the four broad categories describing why some people's efforts complete and others don't? A: Per this teaching: instant completion (favorable planets), delayed-but-eventual completion (partial favor plus sustained ef fort and patience), good start with no finish (some driving force but missing something else), and no real start at all (extremely strong or extremely weak underlying foundation).

Q19. What do "planets" (grah) r epresent in this teaching's framework? A: They are likened to a "government" — an executing body that carries out ef fects, rather than the ultimate source of a person's af flictions.

Q20. Where do doshas (astr ological afflictions) actually originate, per this teaching? A: As a "shraap" (curse) — cosmic ener gy directed by one wronged person at another — which is then registered and carried out through the planetary "government," appearing on a chart as specific doshas.

Q21. Can a planet or dosha lower a person's underlying spiritual "dimension"? A: No — per this teaching, only another person's curse or blessing af fects a person's underlying dimension; planets merely execute what has already been given as part of that curse or blessing.

Q22. What was the speaker's own astr ological situation, according to this account? A: Per this teaching, he describes a heavily afflicted chart — weak Mangal and Chandra, absent Surya and Guru kripa, Kaal Sarp Dosh, and (confirmed live by a community astrologer) a dif ficult Rahu Mahadasha with Shani Antardasha — such that nothing, including his own sadhna, would complete past roughly 30%.

Q23. What did the speaker do after repeatedly failing to complete his efforts at even ordinary tasks? A: Per this teaching, he stopped acting altogether for a time, then turned to jaap (since speech itself is a form of action) — but even jaap stalled at the same ~30% mark.

Q24. What changed once he accepted his 30% limit and r epeated it many times over? A: Per this teaching, he multiplied his 30% effort roughly 300 and then 3,000 times, at which point divine forces ef fectively of fered a partnership — his repeated 30% having become greater than most people's unmultiplied 100%.

Q25. What is the cor e lesson drawn fr om this account? A: Never treat a sadhna as a one-time attempt — if natural capacity is limited, the answer is to repeat the practice as many times as needed rather than to give up.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present the dimensions/parallel-universe/mantra-physics framework (Q8–Q17) as this specific teaching's own esoteric model, not as independently verifiable physics. Present the "30%" astrological account (Q22–Q25) as the speaker's own personal testimony and teaching illustration, not as a claim that can be independently verified. The astrologer named in Q22 (Neelam Shivam) is referenced positively as confirming details live in the session; this is a supportive, non-sensitive mention and does not require anonymization. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 99, Hinglish)
The Sunday Mool Tatva Session: Dimensions, Parallel Universes, and the "30%" Teaching on Karma and Destiny

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept.
Exchange 1 — Requesting a Question Form

Devotee: Bhaiya humare paas jaise application hai, agar ek form ho jisme hum kuch sawaal poochh sake, taaki aap 5-10 minute aake unke jawaab de sako. Hum 150-200 bande meeting mein join karte hain toh ek-ek se sawaal poochna bahut lamba time chala jaayega. Bhaiya: Bahut accha sawaal hai. Hamare pehle app mein yeh provision tha. Hum ise dobara app ke andar rakhenge. Lekin ek doubt bata deta hoon: jis vyakti ko seekhna hai woh kahin se bhi seedha pooch lega, sabke saamne bhi pooch lega, usko sharm nahi hai. Jis vyakti ko ungli karni hai, woh form ke andar ungli karta hai — kyunki agar woh directly poochhega toh shaayad unki pol khul jaaye. Aap direct phone karo, poochho, koi dikkat nahi hai.

Why this is her e: A practical, genuinely useful exchange about how to get questions answer ed, and a candid explanation of why an open anonymous form isn't simply r eopened — useful for setting expectations about how to r each mentors.
Exchange 2 — "V ehicle" of the Mantra

Devotee: Bhaiya, you are saying that distance equals speed times time, so is mantra the vehicle? Because each vehicle will have a dif ferent speed. So how will we be the vehicle that can make the speed more? Bhaiya: Repetition — the repetition makes your speed more. It's not about the mantra, it's about the repetition. The more you repeat, it starts generating. That's why "Jai Siyaram" is a very old mantra — it takes at least one crore japa to awaken it, and then its speed becomes very high.
Why this is her e: A sharp clarifying question that distills the session's cor e physics analogy into a simple, memorable takeaway about why r epetition — not the mantra itself — is what matters.
Exchange 3 — "Why Does My Astrologer Say Nothing Will Complete?"

Bhaiya (r ecounting): Maine apne pandit se poochha, maine kaha mujhe yeh bataiye mujhe karna kya hoga. Unhone kaha beta tu mehnat kar , bahut zyada mehnat lagegi aur kuch hota nahi tere se. Maine unse yeh kaha ki agar aap mujhe bataiye ki mere guru sthan par Mangal aa jaaye toh kripa ho jaayegi kya? Unhone kaha rajyog ban jaayega, par aisa asambhav hai, aisa banta nahi. Bhaiya: Mujhe pata tha mera 30% hi kaam hoga... maine 30 ko 300 baar kiya, phir bhi nahi ruka. Ek samay aaya jab is 30% ke andar itni shakti ho gayi ki mujhe 100% par jaane ki zaroorat hi nahi hai.

Why this is her e: The session's central teaching moment — a first-person account, in the speaker's own wor ds, of turning a structurally limited chart into a workable path thr ough r epetition rather than r esignation. Dir ectly useful for anyone who feels their efforts structurally can't succeed.
Note on Curation

Most of this session is either a repeated technical lecture (the dimensions/mantra-physics framework, already covered in Part I and Part II) or an extended personal narrative (the "30%" astrology story), both better represented in full detail in Part I. Only the exchanges with independent, standalone conversational value are included here. The long roll-call-style confirmations of "ji bhaiya" and similar affirmations throughout the lecture are not reproduced, as they carry no independent content.
Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
